flags.name: England
flags.about: Country in north-west Europe, part of the United Kingdom
flags.story: The national flag of England, a constituent country of the United Kingdom, is derived from Saint George's Cross. The association of the red cross as an emblem of England can be traced back to the Late Middle Ages when it was gradually, increasingly, used alongside the Royal Banner.

flags.name: Hong Kong
flags.about: City and special administrative region of China
flags.story: The Regional Flag of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China depicts a white stylised five-petal Hong Kong orchid tree flower in the centre of a Chinese red field.

credit.artist: Designed by Tao Ho SVG code of 24 November 2005 version copied from Open Clip Art SVG code

flags.name: Scotland
flags.about: Country in north-west Europe, part of the United Kingdom
flags.story: The flag of Scotland is the national flag of Scotland, which consists of a white saltire over a blue field. The Saltire, rather than the Royal Standard of Scotland, is the correct flag for all private individuals and corporate bodies to fly.

flags.name: Puerto Rico
flags.about: Unincorporated territory of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Puerto Rico, officially the Flag of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, represents Puerto Rico and its people.

flags.name: Wales
flags.about: Country in north-west Europe, part of the United Kingdom
flags.story: The flag of Wales consists of a red dragon passant on a green and white field. As with many heraldic charges, the exact representation of the dragon is not standardised in law.

credit.artist: Unknown Vector graphics by Tobias Jakobs

flags.name: Macau
flags.about: City and special administrative region of China

flags.name: Martinique
flags.about: Island in the Lesser Antilles, overseas region and department of France
flags.story: The flag of Martinique consists of a red triangle at the hoist, with two horizontal bands, the upper green and the lower black. It was adopted on 2 February 2023. The flag, known as the rouge-vert-noir ("red-green-black"), uses the pan-African colours.

credit.artist: User:MapGrid / User:HapHaxion / User:Femfem5 / User:Triton , based on work by User:Carport

flags.name: New Caledonia
flags.about: French special collectivity and archipelago in Oceania
flags.story: Two flags are in use in the French overseas territory of New Caledonia: the French national flag, which was the only official flag used to represent New Caledonia until 2010, and the flag of Kanak and Socialist National Liberation Front (FLNKS), a Kanak political party favouring independence for New Caledonia.

flags.name: Guam
flags.about: Unincorporated territory of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Guam was adopted on February 9, 1948. The territorial flag is a dark blue field with a narrow red border on all sides. The red border – a later addition – represents the blood spilled during World War II and earlier Spanish sovereignty.

flags.name: Cayman Islands
flags.about: British overseas territory in the Caribbean
flags.story: The flag of the Cayman Islands consists of a Blue Ensign defaced with the British overseas territory's coat of arms. Adopted in 1959 to supplement the Union Jack and to replace the flag of the Colony of Jamaica, it has been the flag of the Cayman Islands since the territory was granted self-government that year.

flags.name: United States Virgin Islands
flags.about: Unincorporated territory of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the United States Virgin Islands was adopted on May 17, 1921. It consists of a simplified version of the coat of arms of the United States between the letters V and I.

credit.artist: Percival Wilson Sparks . sparksfamilyassn.org . Retrieved on 2026-05-26 .

flags.name: Bermuda
flags.about: British overseas territory in the North Atlantic Ocean
flags.story: The flag of the British Overseas Territory of Bermuda as a red ensign was first adopted on 4 October 1910. It is a British Red Ensign with the Union Jack in the upper left corner, and the coat of arms of Bermuda in the lower right.

credit.artist: Version 1: Made by Caleb Moore from the Open Clip Art website and uploaded by Nightstallio

flags.name: Greenland
flags.about: Autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark and world's largest island
flags.story: The flag of Greenland features two equal horizontal bands of white (top) and red (bottom) with a counter-changed red-and-white disc slightly to the hoist side of centre.

flags.name: Faroe Islands
flags.about: North Atlantic archipelago organized as an autonomous constituent country of the Kingdom of Denmark
flags.story: The flag of the Faroe Islands is a Nordic cross on a white field, with a red cross fimbriated in blue. It is part of the Nordic cross tradition and is commonly interpreted as a Christian symbol.

credit.artist: It was made by User:IceKarma (Jeffrey Connell), who released it to the public domain.

flags.name: American Samoa
flags.about: Unincorporated territory of the United States of America, located in the Pacific Ocean
flags.story: The flag of American Samoa consists of a red-edged white triangle pointing towards the hoist charged with a bald eagle clutching a war club and fly-whisk, with dark blue upper and lower triangles. It was adopted in April 1960 to replace the "Stars and Stripes" as the official flag of the territory.

flags.name: Northern Mariana Islands
flags.about: Unincorporated territory of the United States of America, located in the Pacific Ocean
flags.story: The flag of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands was adopted on July 1, 1985, by the Second Northern Marianas Constitution. The NMI flag was originally designed during the year 1985. Later during that year, they finalized the draft of the flag in the last CNMI constitutional convention.

flags.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
flags.about: British overseas territory in the Caribbean
flags.story: The current flag of the Turks and Caicos Islands was adopted on 7 November 1968, and modified in 1999. Prior to this, the islands had several different flags either proposed or utilised.

flags.name: British Virgin Islands
flags.about: British overseas territory in the Caribbean
flags.story: The flag of the British Virgin Islands was adopted by Royal Warrant on 15 November 1960 after the islands were made into a separate British colony. Previously, the territory was administered as part of the British Leeward Islands.

credit.artist: No machine-readable author provided. Dbenbenn assumed (based on copyright claims).

flags.name: Gibraltar
flags.about: British overseas territory on the southern end of the Iberian Peninsula
flags.story: The flag of Gibraltar is an elongated banner of arms based on the coat of arms of Gibraltar, granted by Royal Warrant from Queen Isabella I of Castile on 10 July 1502.

credit.artist: Created on behalf of Isabella I of Castile in 1502; this version uploaded by Denelson83 (

flags.name: Anguilla
flags.about: British overseas territory in the Caribbean
flags.story: The national flag of Anguilla, a British overseas territory, consists of a Blue Ensign with the British flag in the canton, charged with the coat of arms of Anguilla in the fly.

flags.name: Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha
flags.about: British overseas territory in the southern Atlantic Ocean
flags.story: Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha, a British Overseas Territory, does not have its own flag; however, the three administrative divisions do have their own flags:

credit.artist: Original: Acts of Union 1800 Vector: Zscout370

flags.name: Montserrat
flags.about: British overseas territory and island in the Caribbean
flags.story: The flag of Montserrat consists of a Blue Ensign with the British overseas territory's coat of arms. Adopted in 1960 to supplement the Union Jack after the dissolution of the British Leeward Islands the year before, it has been the flag of Montserrat since the territory was granted self-government that year.

flags.name: Falkland Islands
flags.about: Archipelago in the South Atlantic Ocean, and a British Overseas Territory, disputed by Argentina
flags.story: The current flag of the Falkland Islands was adopted on 25 January 1999 and consists of a defaced Blue Ensign, with the Union Flag in the canton and the Falkland Islands coat-of-arms in the fly.

credit.artist: Original: Government of the United Kingdom Vector: Nightstallion and Echando una mano

flags.name: British Indian Ocean Territory
flags.about: British overseas territory in the Indian Ocean
flags.story: The flag of the British Indian Ocean Territory is similar to the flags of other British dependencies and colonies as it has the Union Flag in the upper hoist-side corner. The palm tree and crown are symbols of the territory.

flags.name: Tokelau
flags.about: New Zealand territory in the Pacific Ocean
flags.story: Tokelau, a dependent territory of New Zealand, adopted an official flag in 2009. Previously, the flag of New Zealand was used as the official flag for Tokelau.

flags.name: French Southern and Antarctic Lands
flags.about: Overseas territory of France
flags.story: The flag of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands is a flag representing the overseas territory of France consisting of Adélie Land, the Crozet Islands, the Kerguelen Islands, Saint Paul and Amsterdam Islands, and the Scattered Islands. The flag was adopted on 23 February 2007.

flags.name: Wake Island
flags.about: Coral atoll in the North Pacific Ocean administered by the US and also claimed by the Marshall Islands
flags.story: Wake Island, also known as Wake Atoll, is a coral atoll which is an unincorporated territory of the United States in the Micronesia subregion of the Pacific Ocean. The atoll is composed of three islets – Wake, Wilkes, and Peale Islands – surrounding a lagoon encircled by a coral reef.

flags.name: Pitcairn Islands
flags.about: British overseas territory in the South Pacific
flags.story: Pitcairn Islands is a British Overseas Territory in the southern Pacific Ocean. Consisting of a set of four volcanic islands scattered across several hundred kilometers, three of the four islands are uninhabited.

flags.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
flags.about: British overseas territory in the Southern Atlantic Ocean
flags.story: The flag of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands was granted on 3 October 1985, when the Territory was created. Previously the Territory was a part of the former Falkland Islands Dependencies and used the same flag as the Falklands Islands.

flags.name: British Antarctic Territory
flags.about: Sector of Antarctica claimed by the United Kingdom as one of its British Overseas Territories
flags.story: The flag of the British Antarctic Territory was granted on 21 April 1998. It features the coat of arms granted on 1 August 1963, a year after the British Antarctic Territory, a British Overseas Territory, was created. Previously, the Territory was a part of the Falkland Islands Dependencies and used the same flag.
